sayLines.line: 📖 LEARNED: Tireless Stride (Level 1). You walk like water downhill — no wasted steps, no wasted breath. Every mile costs 15% less.
📖 Your old life taught you things. 1 skill from your past — check your Journal.
📖 Your hands remember: knap a Stone knife (stone + vine) — the oldest tool there is. Find the stone.
📖 Your hands remember: weave cloth (3 plant fiber — strip it from cleared brush), and build a Water Filter (cloth + charcoal from fire ashes). Dirty water doesn't have to stay dirty.

You wake up with dirt in your mouth and blood on your hands that isn't yours. The sky is the wrong color — not sunset-wrong, wound-wrong. Isaac Caruso. Bike messenger. From Columbus, Ohio. That was yesterday. This is now. You have: Mother's Ring, Dispatcher's headset, Wedding ring, Coat button, Trail compass. That's everything you own in this world. Haven. Twelve people. The fire is lit. The stars
A man, maybe 30s: "We've got days of stores, not weeks. The treeline is the pantry now. Learn what's out there."
📓 Journal: Food won't come to Haven. Walk past the treeline — learn what grows out there, bring it back, and get it named at camp.
You tell the others you're heading out. Someone nods. "Come back before dark."
— DAY 1 DAWN — The world wakes. Animals are active.
Filled 1L (clean — Haven well). 3L carried (3kg). (-10 kcal hauling, 1 tick.) Cistern: 24L left.

🔥 Olayemi has been turning something over all evening. Finally: “Owen. The story about what you’re after — we all eat from the same pot here, we don’t get to lie about who’s at it.” It costs Olayemi to say it; you can see the price land.
“You’re right.” Owen doesn’t look up. “I wasn’t belong. I was record. I’m sorry — I wanted a cleaner story than I had.” The fire lets it land. Someone passes Owen the bowl without a word.
People bring you their suspicions, written down. You keep every one.
Karen Martin reads the sky: rain tomorrow, cold.
A woman, maybe 30s, with a burn-scarred forearm will work the garden once each day while at Haven. Other orders take priority.
You step into the Haven hall.

(Talking costs a little energy — 10 kcal a conversation. Small talk is cheap; going deep costs time, not more food.)

"Ivy," they say, touching their chest. "I'm Ivy." You'll remember that.
